Title: Word of the Day: Gargantuan — Meaning, pronunciation, origin, and real-world examples
Synopsis: Word of the Day: Gargantuan - This word has a delightfully literary origin. It comes from Gargantua, the giant king in François Rabelais' 16th-century satirical novel Gargantua and Pantagruel (1534). Gargantua was famous for his enormous appetite and physical size — at birth, he supposedly cried so loudly it was heard across the land. His name likely derives from the Spanish/Portuguese word garganta, meaning throat, which also gives us the English word gargle. By the late 1500s, "gargantuan" had entered English as a general adjective for anything of extraordinary magnitude. Gargantuan means extremely large or enormous. Bigger than massive.

Title: ET Prime Special Series: Multibagger or IBC - Part 37: How this auto ancillary is fastening its seatbelt for the EV race
Synopsis: This deep dive follows an auto ancillary company that scaled steadily in its core segment over decades, then began recalibrating as electric mobility started changing procurement priorities for OEMs. The core revenue pool remains primarily OEM-driven, with close to 90% coming from them, and a diversified end-user base. Since 2020, the company has expanded into EV-oriented areas. The piece unpacks how the company is building capability, where the near-term demand sits, and what could shape its next leg. This series on auto ancillary companies works with the assumption that, from the whole set of auto ancillary companies, some multibagger stocks will emerge. And some companies in this space risk going bankrupt.

Title: These large- and mid-cap stocks can give more than 38% return in 1 year, according to analysts
Synopsis: If one looks at the overall performance of the market in the past few months, there have been phases where large-caps have underperformed while mid-caps have outperformed and vice-versa. In this context, it would probably be better to have a combination of large- and mid-cap stocks in your long-term investing portfolio and your trading portfolio. This would be a better mix given that the volatility quotient of the market is likely to remain high over the next couple of months or more. Another factor to keep in mind: Diversification is the key. Why? Because there are sectors which will see cyclical tail and headwinds, not because of anything else but the fact that every industry goes through it.

Title: 52 places to go in 2025
Synopsis: The article showcases diverse global destinations with unique experiences and recent developments. From Jane Austen's anniversary celebrations in England to the reopening of the Alishan Forest Railway in Taiwan, these destinations offer rich cultural explorations. It highlights future events like the Year of Cézanne in France and WorldPride in Washington, D.C.

Title: ET Prime Special: How companies manipulate government incentives and create a false picture
Synopsis: Governments provide incentives and subsidies to companies to promote investment, production, employment, and broader economic development. Accounting standards prescribe how such benefits should be recognised in financial statements. But these very rules are sometimes bent, misused, or selectively interpreted by companies to serve management intent and mislead investors.

Title: The Charlie Kirk purge: How 600 Americans were punished in a pro-Trump crackdown
Synopsis: Following an assassination attempt on Charlie Kirk, over 600 Americans faced job loss or disciplinary action for their online comments. This included criticism of Kirk's politics and views on gun rights. The backlash, fueled by social media campaigns and prominent Republican figures, has led to legal challenges and widespread fear among those who spoke out.

Title: US tech companies enabled the surveillance and detention of hundreds of thousands in China
Synopsis: An AP investigation reveals how American tech companies helped build China's surveillance state, enabling human rights abuses. U.S. firms sold billions in technology to Chinese police and government, despite warnings of its use to suppress dissent and target minorities, particularly in Xinjiang.

Title: US tech companies enabled the surveillance and detention of hundreds of thousands in China
Synopsis: An investigation reveals that US tech firms helped build China's surveillance system. Companies sold technology to Chinese police and government. This aided human rights abuses, including in Xinjiang. Predictive policing was brought to China. This allowed preemptive detentions. American technology formed the base for China's surveillance apparatus. Concerns remain about where sold technology will end up.

Title: These large-caps have ‘strong buy’ & ‘buy’ recos and an upside potential of more than 30%
Synopsis: True, there’s no guessing President Trump's next statement or move. But global markets now seem to sense that the US might find it tough to maintain its high pitch in the tariff war for much longer, resulting in some sort of a rally. As far as the Indian markets are concerned, there is a clear change in trend, with bulls in control on most days. Our assumption is that, with the Q4 earnings season being better in many cases, the chances are that bulls will be on a firmer footing. But do continue to be cautious and selective. In fact, that should guide all investing in emerging markets like India.
